identity.title: Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit
identity.issuer: Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, Northwest Region

scan.summary: This is an air discharge permit issued by Oregon DEQ authorizing Cascade Specialty Chemicals to operate two packed-bed wet scrubbers and solvent storage tanks with carbon adsorption at its Portland facility. The permit sets operating conditions, monitoring requirements, and reporting obligations for the chemical storage and repackaging operation with vapor control. The permit expires November 15, 2026, and operation without renewal after that date is a violation.
scan.freshness_note: Permit expires November 15, 2026, which is 52 days away from today (September 25, 2026). Renewal application was due July 18, 2026—51 days ago. If the company did not submit a timely and complete renewal application by that date, it is now operating in violation of the permit. Request immediate confirmation of whether a timely renewal application was submitted, and if not, contact Oregon DEQ immediately.

conditions.title: Operate sources per permit conditions and Department rules
conditions.evidence_expected: All required records and logs showing compliance with conditions in Sections 2–5

conditions.title: Maintain pressure drop across scrubbers S-1 and S-2 within 2.0 to 6.0 inches of water column when operating
conditions.evidence_expected: Scrubber log with daily pressure drop readings for each operating day

conditions.title: Inspect scrubber components quarterly
conditions.evidence_expected: Scrubber log entries showing date, inspector name, and any corrective actions for recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing, and mist eliminator for each scrubber at least once per calendar quarter

conditions.title: Replace carbon in adsorption unit C-1 at least annually or upon breakthrough detection
conditions.evidence_expected: Records of each carbon replacement date and weekly detector-tube check results at C-1 outlet

conditions.title: Limit visible emissions to 20 percent opacity
conditions.evidence_expected: Records of opacity observations; violations would be any period exceeding 20 percent opacity for more than three minutes in any one hour

conditions.title: Submit annual report by February 15 covering prior calendar year
conditions.evidence_expected: Annual report including total throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon replacement dates, and any excess emission events

conditions.title: Submit semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
conditions.evidence_expected: Semi-annual monitoring report for first half of year submitted by July 31

conditions.title: Maintain all records for at least five years and provide to Department on request
conditions.evidence_expected: All records required by permit kept for minimum five years from date of record and made available upon Department request

conditions.title: Minimize emissions during scrubber malfunction and stop associated line until repaired
conditions.evidence_expected: Records showing reasonable steps taken, including line shutdown during any scrubber malfunction period

conditions.title: Notify Department within 24 hours and report within 15 days of any deviation from permit conditions
conditions.evidence_expected: Phone or email notification within 24 hours of discovery, followed by written report within 15 days describing deviation, cause, duration, and corrective action

conditions.title: Pay annual permit fee by due date on Department invoice
conditions.evidence_expected: Proof of payment of annual permit fee invoiced by Department by the invoice due date

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on all identity, condition, and deadline information—these are stated directly in the permit document and are clear. High confidence on the permit expiry and renewal deadline dates. The status of the renewal application is uncertain: condition 1.3 requires submission by July 18, 2026, which has passed. The permit states that timely submission allows continued operation until final action. Without evidence that a timely application was submitted, the company may currently be operating without a valid permit. This is the single most critical item to verify immediately. All other conditions, records requirements, and monitoring obligations are clearly stated and verifiable against the permit text.
